text: Sir Vaughan Frederick Randal Jones (31 December 1952 – 6 September 2020) was a New Zealand mathematician renowned for his contributions to von Neumann algebras and knot polynomials. He received the Fields Medal in 1990. Born in Gisborne, New Zealand, on 31 December 1952, Jones was raised in Cambridge, New Zealand, where he attended St Peter's School. He later transferred to Auckland Grammar School after winning the Gillies Scholarship and graduated from Auckland Grammar in 1969. He completed his undergraduate studies at the University of Auckland, earning a BSc in 1972 and an MSc in 1973. For his doctoral studies, he moved to Switzerland and completed his PhD at the University of Geneva in 1979, with his thesis titled "Actions of finite groups on the hyperfinite II1 factor" under the supervision of André Haefliger, which earned him the Vacheron Constantin Prize. In 1980, Jones moved to the United States, where he taught at the University of California, Los Angeles (1980–1981) and the University of Pennsylvania (1981–1985), before being appointed professor of mathematics at the University of California, Berkeley, a position he held from 1985 to 2011. His groundbreaking work on knot polynomials, specifically the discovery of the Jones polynomial, originated in the theory of von Neumann algebras, an area already advanced by Alain Connes, and led to solutions of several classical problems in knot theory, increased interest in low-dimensional topology, and the emergence of quantum topology. From 2011 until his death, he served as Stevenson Distinguished Professor of mathematics at Vanderbilt University, while remaining Professor Emeritus at the University of California, Berkeley and a Distinguished Alumni Professor at the University of Auckland. In 1992, he was made an honorary vice-president for life of the International Guild of Knot Tyers. The Royal Society of New Zealand established the Jones Medal in 2010 in his honor. Jones met his wife, Martha Myers, during a ski camp for foreign students in Switzerland; she was a Fulbright scholar and later became an associate professor of medicine, health and society; the couple has three children. Jones died on 6 September 2020 at the age of 67 due to health complications from a severe ear infection. He was also a certified barista.
